title: Tool parameter JSON guardrails and localized error mapping playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current tool/function calling surface accepts a wide variety of JSON parameter shapes across SDKs. Customers report inconsistent error messages when params are invalid (opaque schema errors, no recovery hint, English-only), which increases support load and slows adoption for non-English teams. We need a spec and playbook that standardizes a JSON schema format for tool params, defines runtime validation/coercion policies, and produces localized, actionable error objects across SDKs and the Console.

Goals:
- Define a single, expressive JSON schema flavor (a constrained subset) for authoring tool parameter manifests that is easy to author from PRDs and UI editors.
- Runtime validation rules and coercion modes (strict / permissive / protective) with clear telemetry tags.
- Deterministic error model with machine-readable codes, recovery hints, and user-facing localized messages.
- SDK mappings and graceful compatibility layer for older manifests.
- Console integration for previewing example errors and common remediation suggestions.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full JSON Schema draft-07 capabilities (we intentionally limit complexity).
- Automatic model-side docstring generation for param docs (separate task).

Proposal summary:
1) Schema format: adopt a constrained schema we call "ToolParam v1". It supports: type, required, enum, pattern, min/max, default, example, description (markdown), and union via "oneOf" limited to max 3 branches. It disallows arbitrary "additionalProperties" unless explicitly opt-in. This keeps manifests compact and machine-friendly.
2) Validation/coercion: runtime will support three modes: 
   - strict: reject any type mismatch or unexpected keys (default for enterprise).
   - permissive: attempt lightweight coercions (string->number, numeric strings), ignore unknown keys but log telemetry.
   - protective: accept extra keys but attach warnings and sanitize potentially harmful values.
   Mode is configurable per-route and inherits from project or org settings.
3) Error model: errors emitted by the runtime conform to an error envelope: {"code":"TP_PARAM_TYPE_MISMATCH","field":"items.quantity","message":"Localized message","hint":"Try passing an integer between 1 and 100","meta":{"expected":"integer","received":"string"}}. We will map this into SDK exceptions and Console UI cards. Errors MUST include: stable code, field path, short hint, and example when applicable.
4) Localization: maintain a central i18n file for each stable message template. Telemetry will log message key + code so translations can be updated without changing codes. Fallback to English if translation not available.
5) Backcompat: runtime will attempt to auto-upgrade legacy manifests by injecting "additionalProperties":true if legacy_compat flag set. A migration linter will run in CI and show warnings in the Console.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Restricting schema expressivity reduces author flexibility but dramatically improves consistent validation and error localisation across languages.
- Three-mode validation offers a pragmatic path for enterprise customers needing strictness and for public hosted API users preferring forgiving behavior.
- Including actionable hints increases UX payoff but requires author discipline to include good examples in manifests. We'll provide a manifest linter and a small suggested hint generator for common cases.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize ToolParam v1 spec, i18n keys, and error code taxonomy. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/TOOL/ToolParam+v1+Spec)
- Week 2: Implement schema parser and validator in runtime (Go) + validation mode flag support.
- Week 3: SDK mappings (Python/JS/Go): convert error envelope to exceptions with localized message hooks.
- Week 4: Console preview UI card + CI linter integration.
- Week 5: Canary rollout for small subset of routes and gather telemetry.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Authors omit hints -> poor UX. Mitigation: Linter enforces minimal hint or example for any parameter without obvious constraints.
- Risk: Translations lag. Mitigation: Log message keys and surface missing locales in Console. Provide default English hint and require security review for message content.

Docs / artifacts: design doc (Confluence), mockups, PRs listed below.

acceptance_criteria: Runtime parses ToolParam v1 and validates example manifest without runtime exceptions in CI
Error envelope produced for invalid params contains stable code, field path, hint, and meta with expected/received types
SDKs map envelope to user-friendly exceptions and expose localized messages if client requests locale
Console shows preview of validation errors for a given manifest and sample request
Telemetry emits tp.validation.failure for every rejected request and includes reason code and validation mode
